---
title: Single-binary compilation
description: Compile your seedcord bot into one binary to run it on a server without a JavaScript runtime.
---

<Callout type="note">

This section is not applicable to edge builds.

</Callout>

Depending on what runtime you're using, you have two options:

## Bun single-file executable

Bun comes built-in with its own compiler to generate a standalone binary.

In order to compile with Bun, use the following command:

```sh
bun run build # Builds your bot first
bun build ./dist/index.mjs --compile --outfile bot # bot.exe on Windows
```

Cross-compiling should use the `--target` flag. Read the [Bun documentation](https://bun.sh/docs/compiler/executables) to learn more about single-file executable compilation.

## Node.js SEA (Single-Executable Application)

<Callout type="note">

This section assumes Node.js 26+ for its simplicity. You'll need to follow different instructions for Node.js [24](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/single-executable-applications.html).

</Callout>

<Callout type="warn">

We recommend not configuring compiling with Node.js SEA directly, due to certain limitations. We hope these limitations get resolved in the future.

Instead, read the ["Other tools that build executables on Node"](#other-tools-that-build-executable-on-node) section for tools that manage this instead.
These all require Node 26+.

</Callout>

You can compile your bot to a single binary using Node.js SEA.

Due to current limitations at the time of writing, to properly compile your bot using SEA, you'll need to re-bundle your bot to be a singular file. Use a bundler like `esbuild`:

```sh
npm run build # use the build command with your package manager
npx esbuild --bundle dist/index.mjs --outfile=bin/index.js --platform=node --format=esm
```

Create a SEA configuration file:

```jsonc
// Node.js does not accept JSONC; remove comments before usage.
{
    "main": "bin/index.js",
    "mainFormat": "module",
    "output": "bot" // On Windows, set this to bot.exe
}
```

Then, use Node to compile the binary:

```sh
node --build-sea sea-config.json
```

And now you have a compiled executable with your seedcord bot.

You can also bundle assets in and use them via the `node:sea` built-in module. Read the [Node.js documentation on SEA](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/single-executable-applications.html) to learn more about SEA compilation.

### Other tools that build executables on Node

- tsdown has built-in support to compile Node apps via SEA [(docs)](https://tsdown.dev/options/exe). This is the recommended option if you are already using Vite+ as, with the right configuration, you can run `seedcord build` and then `vp pack` to generate binaries for all platforms.
- `pkg` is a (now-deprecated, but has active forks) CLI for compiling Node apps via its own mechanism (independent of SEA).
